notes: Built from the 1715 map, adjusted to 1750.
Iran: Nader Shah ended the Safavids (1736); after his murder (1747) Ahmad Shah Durrani founded the Durrani Empire in Afghanistan.
India: the Mughal emperor still reigned in Delhi, but the Marathas held most of the Deccan, Malwa and Gujarat, and the nawabs of Bengal, Awadh and Hyderabad ruled their provinces independently.
Europe: Prussia took Silesia (1742); Russia gained the eastern Baltic from Sweden (1721); Naples and Sicily formed a Bourbon kingdom (1735); Sardinia passed to Savoy (1720).
North America: British colonies from Maine to Georgia; French Canada on the St Lawrence and Louisiana on the lower Mississippi. Many interior nations remained independent.
West Africa: Asante and Dahomey expanded in the age of the Atlantic slave trade.
Not yet drawn: Qing control of Tibet (from 1720) and the Rajput, Sikh and Rohilla states; the Habsburgs lost northern Serbia to the Ottomans in 1739.
